title: Describe an automation in plain words and let IFTTT's AI build and run it
summary: IFTTT ("if this, then that") is now IFTTT.ai. You type what you want, like "when a package is delivered, flash my lights" or "email me when it's going to rain tomorrow", and it builds the automation and runs it around the clock. Its new AI Agent can also watch a web page for new items, or act across your connected apps from a plain-language instruction.
what_the_bot_does: You describe the job in IFTTT's chat (or ask Claude or ChatGPT, which can connect to IFTTT).
It builds an Applet: one clear trigger ("if this") and one or more actions ("then that") across 1,000+ apps and devices.
The trigger can be something happening, like a new email, a delivery, a weather change, or a new item showing up on a web page you pick.
When it fires, the action runs: a notification, a calendar event, a row in a spreadsheet, a smart-home change, or an AI step that writes a summary or message.
An activity page shows every run, including what it skipped and why, and you can switch any Applet off with one tap.
what_you_end_up_with: Small always-on helpers that react the moment something happens, built by describing them, with a clear trigger and action you can read and turn off.

tools.note: Unlimited Applets and all services on the Free plan since Oct 28, 2026; runs use monthly credits
Optional: connect IFTTT under Settings > Connectors
Optional: connect IFTTT as an app

prompt: Build me an IFTTT Applet: when [a new email arrives from my kid's school / it's going to rain tomorrow / a new job is posted on this page: URL], then [send me a phone notification / add an event to my Google Calendar / add a row to my Google Sheet] with [what it should say]. Use only the apps I've already connected. Show me the trigger and action in plain words before you turn it on, and don't add any step that sends a message to someone else.
setup: Make a free account at ifttt.com and install the IFTTT app on your phone if you want notifications.
Open IFTTT's chat and describe one small job in a sentence. Or start from a ready-made Applet in Explore.
Connect only the services that Applet needs (for example Gmail and Notifications). IFTTT asks you to sign in to each one on its own page.
Read the trigger and action it shows you, then turn it on. Check the activity page after the first few runs.
Optional: in Claude (Settings > Connectors) or ChatGPT, add IFTTT so you can say "turn on the Applet that..." from your chat.
watch_out: Runs now use credits. The Free plan has 1,000 a month; when they run out your Applets pause until next month (nothing is deleted). Paid plans start at $2.09 a month billed yearly (IFTTT plans page, Oct 29, 2026).
On Free, IFTTT checks for new triggers only once an hour (every 15 minutes on Starter, 5 on Pro), so it's not for things that need a second-by-second reaction.
Some shop and web pages that load with JavaScript don't work with the page-watching trigger yet (IFTTT launch guide, per HiTecWeb).
An AI action can send messages or post for you. Keep actions to notifications, your own calendar and your own sheets until you trust it.
